description: A lightweight 2.5D character player for the web, with lip sync and webcam face tracking.
readme_excerpt:
A lightweight 2.5D character player for the web, with lip sync and webcam face tracking. A few lines of code put a character in a page, a stream overlay or an app.
Comes with 21 featured characters in different styles, ready to use.

English · 中文 · 日本語 · Tiếng Việt

- WebGL2, no dependencies, about 30 KB gzipped for the core - Lip sync (microphone, audio, video) and webcam face tracking (MediaPipe), both in the browser, imported only when you need them - Plays LivLiv, VRM and PNGTuber characters through the same API - 21 featured characters in [`characters/`](characters/), ready to use ## Try it - **Online**: the examples run on [livliv-dev.github.io/player](https://livliv-dev.github.io/player/). - **Here**: `npm install && npm run build`, serve this folder with any static server and open `/example/demo.html` (expressions, actions, microphone, camera; `?model=../characters//` picks another character). `/example/png.html` and `/example/vrm.html` show a PNGTuber and a VRM. - **On livliv.ai**: each character's page there plays it with the same renderer. Start at [livliv.ai/discover](https://livliv.ai/discover). ## Project LivLiv We want the art of creating characters to belong to everyone. We're open-sourcing our AI tools for character creation, the player and its playback protocol, and a stage where your characters can meet an audience. Come say hello on [Discord](https://discord.gg/ac5qF36T2H) and follow us on [X (Twitter)](https://x.com/livliv_ai). ## Use it in your page ```sh npm install @livliv-dev/player ``` ```js import { Player } from '@livliv-dev/player' const player = new Player(document.querySelector('canvas')) await player.load('characters/k01/') // a folder with model.json and textures/, or a .livliv file player.setExpression('smile') // ids are in player.expressions player.act('nod') player.params.mouthOpen = 0.6 // 0..1 ``` Lip sync and face tracking: ```js import { createSpeech } from '@livliv-dev/player/voice' import { startFaceTracking } from '@livliv-dev/player/tracking' // needs @mediapipe/tasks-vision const speech = createSpeech(player) button.onclick = () => { speech.unlock(); speech.say('/reply.mp3') } await startFaceTracking(player) ``` A VRM or a PNGTuber, on the same API: ```js import { BodyPlayer } from '@livliv-dev/player/body' import { VrmBody } from '@livliv-dev/player/vrm' // needs three and @pixiv/three-vrm import { PngBody } from '@livliv-dev/player/png' const vrm = new BodyPlayer(canvasA, new VrmBody()) await vrm.load('/avatars/me.vrm') const png = new BodyPlayer(canvasB, new PngBody()) await png.load({ closed: 'me-closed.png', open: 'me-open.png' }) ``` The whole API is in [API.md](API.md): options, params, expressions and actions, drivers, VRM and PNGTuber characters, the limits on untrusted files, the model package and the format version. The LivLiv package format (`.livliv`, `model.json` v4) is in [FORMAT.md](FORMAT.md), with a JSON Schema in [`schema/`](schema/); packages exported before v4 are described in [FORMAT-v3.md](FORMAT-v3.md) and still play. > The npm package is the player alone. The featured characters are in this repository's [`characters/`](characters/): copy > the ones you use next to your page, with their licence. ## Featured characters `characters/` holds 21 characters, ready to `load()`. They carry a small LivLiv mark in the bottom-right corner, which the player draws. They are **not** covered by the Apache L

description: A GPU task manager for Windows, Linux, and WSL: per-process VRAM, GPU activity, and LLM model/KV-cache insights (Windows AMD and NVIDIA).
readme_excerpt:
# gputaskman

**An `htop` for what's inside your GPU, not just how full it is.**

Windows + NVIDIA/AMD, with Linux and WSL support (NVIDIA everywhere, AMD and Intel on native Linux; see
[Linux and WSL](#linux-and-wsl)) and macOS on Apple Silicon (see [macOS](#macos-apple-silicon)). A terminal UI
that connects per-process GPU memory and engine activity with loaded runtimes, model files, and
LLM buffer breakdowns.

Task Manager says "15 GB used." This tries to answer: *by what? Model weights? KV cache?
Your browser? The desktop compositor? And why is so much GPU memory in system RAM?*

**Scope: local GPU workloads, not cloud services.** Decision models, vision, speech, LLM inference,
training/fine-tuning (including Unsloth), graphics, and video all belong here. Visibility varies:
process memory and engine activity are measured; identifying individual models and their work
requires supporting evidence. A PyTorch/CUDA DLL alone cannot identify a model or prove training,
and a mapped file does not prove that model is resident on the GPU or being exercised.
CPU-only, NPU-only, and cloud workloads are out of scope.

![Live GPU overview with an LLM's weights, KV cache, and compute buffer breakdown](docs/screenshots/overview.png)

> Early, experimental software. Device and process counters are measurements; classifications
> and GGUF-derived breakdowns are estimates. This does not dump VRAM or enumerate a game's textures.

## Install from PyPI

[gputaskman is on PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/gputaskman/). No repository clone is needed:

```powershell
uv tool install gputaskman
gputaskman
```

Or, with [pipx](https://pipx.pypa.io/):

```powershell
pipx install gputaskman
gputaskman
```

Works on Windows, Linux/WSL, and macOS with Python 3.11+ and the supported GPU/driver
configuration described below. Both installers keep the app in an isolated environment.
The shorter `gtm` command is also available. Upgrade with `uv tool upgrade gputaskman`
or `pipx upgrade gputaskman`. For Windows without Python, use the portable download below.

## Portable Windows download

The [Releases page](https://github.com/shanselman/gputaskman/releases) is where tagged builds
publish two portable ZIPs: `gputaskman-VERSION-windows-x64.zip` for Intel/AMD Windows PCs, and
`gputaskman-VERSION-windows-arm64.zip` for native Windows ARM64. These are separate native builds,
not a universal executable.

Extract the **entire ZIP**, keeping `_internal` beside `gputaskman.exe`. Open Windows Terminal
or PowerShell in the extracted folder:

```powershell
.\gputaskman.exe
.\gputaskman.exe --once
.\gputaskman.exe --json
```

No Python, uv, CUDA Toolkit, model download, or installation is needed. A supported GPU with a
current Windows WDDM driver is required. Builds are currently **unsigned**; code signing
and an installer are not part of this initial distribution. Each ZIP includes licenses and a
`.zip.sha256` companion file is published for integrity checks.

## Clone and run

Use **64-bit Windows 10/11**, an **NVIDIA or AMD GPU with a current WDDM driver**, and a terminal
(Windows Terminal is recommended). Live workload checks have included an RTX 4080 SUPER and an
RTX Spark N1X on Windows ARM64. CUDA workloads are supported on ARM64 with a compatible NVIDIA
driver and ARM64 CUDA runtime.

AMD live check: Radeon 860M Graphics on Windows 11 Enterprise build 26300, AMD driver 32.0.22050.1003.
During desktop/browser activity, WDDM reported per-process VRAM and AMD ADL reported GPU utilization,
clocks, and ASIC power; temperature, memory activity, and PCIe readings were unavailable. Vulkan/ROCm
workloads were not tested on this machine.

Install [Git for Windows](https://git-scm.com/downloads/win) and
[uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/) if needed. With WinGet:

```powershell
winget install --id Git.Git --exact
winget install --id astral-sh.uv --exact
```

Open a new PowerShell window so those tools are on `PATH`, then:

```powershell
git clone https

description: A native music player you extend with plugins
readme_excerpt:
# MyGo Music

A native desktop music player written in Go with [MyGo](https://github.com/egoist/mygo), no WebView. It plays your local files out of the box, and everything else comes from plugins.

## Features

- Local files (MP3, FLAC, Ogg Vorbis, WAV, and ALAC, FLAC or AAC in .m4a and .aac) with tags, covers and `.lrc` lyrics
- Playlists, liked songs, search, albums and artists
- Now Playing with lyric stage styles, cover wall, queue, shuffle and repeat
- Notch player on macOS, tray, media keys
- Audio cache, fades on pause and seek, loudness normalization
- Session restore
- Podcast captions, written down on the device as episodes play
- English and Simplified Chinese
- Plugins can add accounts, catalogs, podcasts, stations, comments and pages of their own

## Build

```bash
go tool mygo dev     # run in development
go tool mygo build   # package into build/
go test ./internal/...
```

## Podcast captions

Episodes are written down on the device as they play, with [sherpa-onnx](https://github.com/k2-fsa/sherpa-onnx) and Qwen3-ASR, which the app downloads when the listener asks for them. The libraries come from this repository's `sherpa-onnx-<version>` prerelease, which only changes with that version:

```bash
go run ./scripts/sherpa -sign "Developer ID Application: …"
gh release create sherpa-onnx-2.0.1 --prerelease --latest=false build/sherpa/*
```

## Plugins

A plugin is a folder in the app's `plugins` directory (Settings > Plugins > + > Show Plugins Folder) with a `plugin.json` and one JavaScript or TypeScript file. Install one with the + in Settings > Plugins from GitHub, by its repository or its address, or from its folder or a zip of it on this computer, or drop the folder in by hand. Remove one from its ⋯ menu there. There's nothing to build, and the same plugin runs on every platform. [`examples/demo-plugin`](examples/demo-plugin) does everything a plugin can with made-up data: copy it to start.

```json
{
  "id": "example",
  "name": "Example",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "minAppVersion": "0.1.8",
  "main": "index.js",
  "playback": "stream",
  "permissions": { "network": ["api.example.com"] },
  "settings": [{ "key": "apiKey", "label": "API Key", "help": "From your account page", "link": "https://example.com/keys" }],
  "navigation": [
    { "builtin": "home" },
    { "title": "Charts", "page": "charts", "icon": "chart" },
    { "title": "Stations", "builtin": "stations" }
  ]
}
```

```js
export async function search({ query, kind, offset }) {
  const res = await fetch(`https://api.example.com/search?q=${encodeURIComponent(query)}&type=${kind}&offset=${offset}`, {
    headers: { authorization: `Bearer ${host.setting("apiKey")}` },
  });
  return { tracks: (await res.json()).items.map(toTrack), more: false };
}

export function stream({ id, quality }) {
  return { url: `https://api.example.com/audio/${id}.mp3`, type: "mp3" };
}
```

Export a function for each thing the plugin does. Each takes one object of parameters and returns a value or a promise. What it doesn't export, the app leaves out of its pages.

| Export | Parameters | Returns |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `signIn`, `signOut`, `account` | | `{id, name, imageUrl, page}`; `account` returns `null` when signed out. `page` is a `browse` page of the listener's own, which the account menu opens as My Page |
| `setSetting` | `{key, value}` | |
| `home` | | `Browse` |
| `browse` | `{page}` | `Browse` |
| `search` | `{query, kind, offset}`, where `kind` is `tracks`, `albums`, `artists`, `playlists` or `shows` | `{tracks or albums or ..., more}` |
| `suggest` | `{query}` | `[string]` |
| `recent` | | `[Track]` |
| `played` | `{id}` | |
| `liked` | `{offset}` | `{tracks, more}` |
| `isLiked` | `{ids}` | `{id: bool}` |
| `like`, `likeEpisode` | `{id, on}` | `like` likes a song, and `likeEpisode` an episode: without it, episodes show no heart |
| `album` | `{id}` | `{album, tracks}` |
| `artist` | `{id}` | `{artist, tracks, albums}` |
| `saveAlbum`, `followArtist`, `savePlay

description: the ultimate vocal synthesizer - sing, speak, beatbox, and more
readme_excerpt:
# CHIMERA

A physical-modeling voice synthesizer in the browser. Every sound comes from a simulated
airway (lungs, vocal folds or syrinx, a branched vocal tract, lips, nose), not from samples.
The engine is Rust, compiled to WebAssembly for an AudioWorklet; the same code runs natively
for tests and the `chimera` CLI.

## What it does

- **Play**: drag the tongue, lips and jaw in a live cutaway of the head; vowel pad, encoders,
  computer keyboard and Web MIDI.
- **Speak**: English text (CMUdict with a letter-to-sound fallback) or IPA, turned into
  gestures and prosody, with the gestural score and a consonant chart on screen.
- **Sing**: piano roll with lyrics per note; consonants land before the beat.
- **Beatbox**: pads and a step sequencer, every drum an articulatory gesture.
- **Bestiary**: songbird (two-voice syrinx), seal, alligator and elephant.
- **Duet** (`?show=<id>`): two 3D heads replay a pre-rendered song.

Male, female and child bodies blend continuously. Everything on screen animates from live
engine state: pressure in the airway, airflow, the vocal folds, spectra and formants.

## Run it

Needs Rust with the `wasm32-unknown-unknown` target, and Bun.

```sh
bun install
bun run dev        # builds the wasm, then Vite on 127.0.0.1:5317
bun run test       # wasm build, cargo test --workspace, bun test tests
```

The AudioWorklet needs a secure context, so open it on localhost or over HTTPS (for example
`tailscale serve`). Vercel builds it with `vercel.json`.

Offline renders and measurement:

```sh
cargo run --release -p chimera-cli -- render speech|text|song|notes|beatbox|creature|vowels …
cargo run --release -p chimera-cli -- diagnose       # nasal leakage, formants, bandwidths, pitch
cargo run --release -p chimera-cli -- compare csd    # against a real singer (docs/csd-comparison.md)
cargo run --release -p chimera-cli -- compare tsp    # against 23 real speakers (docs/speech-comparison.md)
bun tools/spectrogram.ts in.wav out.png
```

## Docs

- [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md): the acoustic model (FDTD airway, sources,
  anatomy, gestures).
- [docs/rust-engine.md](docs/rust-engine.md): the engine's real-time and determinism contract,
  and the browser boundary.
- [docs/ui-redesign.md](docs/ui-redesign.md) and [docs/mockups/](docs/mockups/): the vector
  display look.
- [docs/csd-comparison.md](docs/csd-comparison.md): scoring the voice against the Children's
  Song Dataset.
- [docs/speech-comparison.md](docs/speech-comparison.md): scoring the speech against real
  speakers, phone by phone (the TSP speech database).
- [docs/hill-climb/](docs/hill-climb/): the rules and log for tuning the voice one measured
  step at a time.

Agents: see [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md).

## License

[MIT](LICENSE). Bundled third-party files keep their own licenses: the CMU Pronouncing
Dictionary ([public/data/CMUDICT-LICENSE.txt](public/data/CMUDICT-LICENSE.txt)) and the fonts
([public/fonts/](public/fonts/)).

description: 3D modeling in Python, built for LLMs.
readme_excerpt:
sand3d

**3D modeling in Python, built for LLMs.** sand3d is a Python library for writing 3D objects as short programs: profiles, solids, edits, frames, joints and assemblies, over Blender's `bpy`. A program says *how* a shape is made, part by part and in its own words, so a model writes it in a few hundred tokens and a person can read it.

 Website ·  Docs ·  Datasets ·  Explorer

## Why sand3d


How it is measured, part by part

- **Short.** A part takes 2 to 6× fewer tokens than the same part in Blender Python, CadQuery or FeatureScript ([details](https://sand3d.sandflow.ai/tokens.html)). - **The whole API fits in a prompt**, about 3,600 tokens ([the API](https://sand3d.sandflow.ai/api.html)). - **Named, not computed.** Parts, edges and faces are reached by name, never by hand-computed coordinates. - **Deterministic.** The same program builds the same mesh, bit for bit. ## A whole object, part by part

A front-loading washing machine in 38 lines of code ([play it and read it](https://sand3d.sandf

# Agent skills from Jane Street

A collection of skills for AI agents and chatbots.
Each skill is a directory containing a `SKILL.md` file
with instructions for the agent.

## Skills

- **socratic-tutor** — turns an LLM into a strict personal tutor that teaches a
  topic of your choice using the Socratic method: a diagnostic, a skill map with
  levels 0-5, one question at a time, spaced review, and a final assessment.

## How to use

With a coding agent that supports the common `SKILL.md` format, copy the skill
directory into your agent's skills folder, then ask the agent to use it
("teach me X").

With a plain chatbot, paste the body of the skill's `SKILL.md` into the chat
(or into a custom/system prompt), followed by what you want it to do.

description: Emulate macOS on iOS and iPadOS
readme_excerpt:
Henge

macOS on your iPhone and iPad.

Install · How it works · Website · Releases

Download macOS, install it on the device, and use it. - **Own emulator** — iOS gives apps no hypervisor, so Henge runs the Mac's arm64 code through its own JIT, with its own MMU and devices. It doesn't use QEMU or Virtualization.framework. - **Installs on the device** — Henge downloads Apple's restore image and restores it the way a Mac does. No Mac needed, and nothing is decrypted or patched. - **Graphics** — macOS draws through a virtual GPU, and Henge replays its commands with Metal. Safari and Electron apps like Discord draw on it. - **Touch** — The screen is a trackpad: hold to drag, two fingers to scroll. Esc, Tab, Control, Option and Command sit above the keyboard. - **Keyboard and mouse** — On iPad, a Magic Keyboard or a Bluetooth keyboard and mouse drive the Mac directly. - **External display** — During a Mac session, connect a display with a video-capable USB-C cable or a USB-C/HDMI dock. The mode activates automatically: the monitor shows the Mac, while the iPhone or iPad keeps its trackpad and keyboard controls. Disconnect to return the image to the device. The existing guest resolution is preserved. On iOS 17–26 the same happens through an older iOS route, not yet tried on hardware; outside a Mac session the display mirrors the device. USB-C video is user-confirmed on an iPhone 17 Pro running iOS 27 (development build 0.1/2). - **Sharing** — Copy and paste between macOS and the device, and a shared folder that shows up in Files and on the Mac. - **Fits the screen** — On iPad, a new Mac gets a screen the shape of the iPad's, so there are no black bars. On an iPhone 17 Pro, macOS reaches the lock screen in about 15 seconds. Discord installs, opens in about 15 seconds, logs in and sends messages. ## Install Sideload `Henge.ipa` from [Releases](https://github.com/Leviidev/Henge/releases) with SideStore or AltStore, or install `Henge.tipa` with TrollStore or TrollStore Lite. iOS or iPadOS 17 or later, on an A14 or M1 chip or newer. So far it's tested only on an iPhone 17 Pro: iPad support is new and hasn't run on a real iPad yet. - **JIT** is required: StikDebug, TrollStore (which stops at iOS 17.0), TrollStore Lite (which needs a jailbreak), a jailbreak on its own, or the StikJIT helper built into Henge (iOS 26 or later). - **Storage:** about 43 GB free for macOS Sequoia. That's 17 GB for the download, which you can delete afterwards, and 26 GB for the Mac. - **Memory:** a Mac gets 4, 6 or 8 GB. Sign Henge with the increased memory limit entitlement if your certificate has it. Then open the Install tab, pick macOS Sequoia 15.6.1, and keep Henge open with the device plugged in. Tahoe 26.6.2 and macOS 27.2 are offered too, but they aren't tested yet. ## Sharing with the Mac Do this once for each Mac: open Terminal on the Mac, then in Henge open Details and tap **Type the Set Up Command**. Press Return on the Mac, and choose Allow when macOS asks about `henge-agent` and local networks. It needs the Mac's keyboard layout to be U.S. Then a Henge folder in the Mac's home folder is the same folder as Files › Henge › Shared. What you copy on the Mac is copied on the device too, and the paste button pastes from the device into the Mac. ## Kn

description: Headless 3D and VFX engine for agents. Research preview.
readme_excerpt: **vork is a 3D and VFX engine built for AI agents.** Agents write the whole scene as code, including their own shaders, materials, cameras and physics, and vork renders it on the GPU. The core API fits in about 2,500 tokens. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/03cfa020-be40-483a-89af-1ef77467b7a0 **One million birds, each on its own path.** 192 frames at 1080p rendered in 97 seconds on a single NVIDIA L4. Blender EEVEE at the same sample count is projected at 13–18 minutes. [How we measured](#million-birds-measured-movies-projected-blender-times) · [how it's made](examples/murmuration/) · [credits](examples/murmuration/CREDITS) - **Built for agents:** a small API that agents can extend with their own GPU programs. - **Fast:** 1.1–2.3× faster than EEVEE on default stills and movies, and about 8–11× on the bird flock. [Speed, with the qualifications](#speed-with-the-qualifications). - **Native GPU engine:** written in Rust and Slang, runs on Vulkan and Metal (Linux, Windows, macOS). ## Paste this to your agent [Install vork](#install), then paste: > Run `vork init my-shot`, read `vork help`, render a preview and inspect the image. > Refine the camera and lighting before rendering at final quality. Read the > relevant help topic when you need a feature the first page doesn't explain. vork is written in Rust and Slang, with GPU rendering through Vulkan and Metal. An agent writes a scene, renders it, looks at the result and revises the code. There is no editor to drive. Most creative tools expose controls that a person can operate. An agent can also write a shader in the middle of a shot. vork gives it geometry, ray queries and GPU execution, then lets scene programs define materials, cameras, light propagation, simulation and compositing. Ordinary shots need only scene data; the programming hooks are there when the shot needs something unusual. Source-available and free during the research preview. ## Start here After [installing vork](#install), create a working project: ```sh vork init my-shot cd my-shot vork render scene.json --out render.png vork help ``` Open `render.png`, change a colour or camera position in `scene.json`, and render again. The starter uses only bundled sphere, box and grid primitives: no downloads, no GPU needed to initialize. Use `vork init my-shot --language typescript` or `--language python` for editable `scene.ts` or `scene.py` alongside the ready-to-render JSON. The generated README explains regeneration and SDK requirements. Existing files are never overwritten. The default `std/final` profile is warmed by setup; use `--profile std/draft` for quicker previews. ## What you can make The examples include code, preparation commands and credits. Large downloaded assets and footage stay outside Git; the recipes fetch them or accept a local path. The images here are stills from these shots. Keep each credit with its image. ### [Million birds](examples/murmuration/) ![A ribbon of starlings crossing the low sun above a lagoon](docs/images/

description: Monitors your RAM and reports any "quite terrible" unused capacity directly to the CEO of OpenAI.
readme_excerpt:
# Ram-Altman

**A bash script that writes to Sam Altman once a day to report the RAM he missed.**

Read the sample emails at **[ram-altman.lol](https://ram-altman.lol)**, no install needed.

[![Website: ram-altman.lol](https://img.shields.io/badge/website-ram--altman.lol-0f5a43)](https://ram-altman.lol)
![Global DRAM allocation: quite terrible](https://img.shields.io/badge/global%20DRAM%20allocation-quite%20terrible-red)
![Utilization: maybe 5%](https://img.shields.io/badge/utilization-maybe%205%25-orange)
![Emails: 1 per day](https://img.shields.io/badge/emails-1%20per%20day-blue)
![Written in Bash, not Electron](https://img.shields.io/badge/written%20in-bash%2C%20not%20electron-brightgreen)

There is RAM in your computer. Right now. Just sitting there, in a *personal* computer, being personal.

You may have thought of this as "a computer working normally". On a recent episode of [Cheeky Pint](https://gizmodo.com/sam-altman-youre-completely-right-about-ram-im-sorry-for-the-confusion-heres-what-happened-2000835208), the CEO of OpenAI offered another view:

> "From a global allocation perspective, actually, it's quite terrible to have everybody have a bunch of the world's limited supply of DRAM sitting in their own computer"
>
> — Sam Altman

That RAM, he added, is ["being used maybe 5% of the time"](https://www.xda-developers.com/sam-altman-says-its-quite-terrible-that-people-have-ram-in-their-pcs-during-a-shortage/).

Which raised an obvious question for a certain kind of person: *surely someone should be monitoring this?*

So we wrote a script. If your machine has more than 10% of its RAM available, it sends one email a day to let Sam know. It seemed only fair. He can't fix the problem if nobody tells him where the RAM is.

## Features

- Tracks total, used and available RAM, plus your standing with the global allocation authorities
- Handles page cache correctly, which already puts it ahead of most arguments about RAM
- Sends at most one email per day, because we're hoarders, not animals
- Rotates 8 subject lines, 10 messages and 6 sign-offs, so the joke gets old at a carefully managed pace
- Logs every sample to CSV for when the auditors arrive
- Ships with 14 tests, more than the DRAM market has had sensible outcomes
- Is written in bash, as an Electron version would have solved the problem by using all the RAM

## A sample of today's correspondence

```text
Subject: You missed a spot

Hi Sam,

Please don't be alarmed, but there is 8.6 GiB of RAM on my desk that isn't in
a data centre. That's 56.2% of what's installed here, and as far as I can tell
it has no plans today.

Hoarding responsibly,
A concerned RAM owner

--
Sent automatically, at most once a day, by a small script on one PC.
Reply if you'd like it to stop.
```

The figures are real. They come from your machine. That's the worrying part.

## What counts as "used"?

```text
used = MemTotal - MemAvailable
```

`MemAvailable` is the kernel's own estimate of how much memory programs could claim without swapping. Free RAM counts as available. So does cache the kernel can reclaim. tmpfs and shared memory don't, because they can't simply be handed back.

Every sysadmin has spent years explaining that [Linux didn't eat your RAM](https://www.linuxatemyram.com/) and that free RAM is wasted RAM. It took decades for someone important to agree with the second part, and he'd like it shipped to him.

Strictly speaking, the page cache is doing useful work, so counting it as available is a generous concession to the other side. Think of it as a plea bargain.

On kernels older than 3.14, which have no `MemAvailable`, the script estimates it from free memory plus reclaimable cache. If you're on one of those, your RAM may be safe. Nobody's coming for that.

## Installation

You'll need Linux, bash, and a working `sendmail`, `msmtp` or `mail` command. Your RAM is assumed.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/IainKay/ram-altman.git
cd ram-altman
chmod +x ram-altman.sh test-ram-altm

# GIF 工厂 [像素与游戏](#pixel-games) · [插画与二次元](#illustration-anime) · [真人与宠物](#people-pets) · [材质与吉祥物](#materials-mascots) · [卡片与变画](#cards-transforms) · [海报与文字](#posters-type) · [品牌短片](#brand-films) · [动态绘本](#storybooks) **挑一种风格，给一张参考图，把角色、相片和想法做成 GIF，也能延伸成动态绘本。** 像素小人、人物与宠物、粘土吉祥物、光栅变画、漫画动态海报。 先看效果，再换成你自己的角色和主题；拿不准就先做一张。 **6 个 GIF 分类 · 10 个 GIF 风格入口 · 65 个动态案例，另有动态绘本和品牌短片** [浏览风格](styles/README.md) · [完整作品库](GALLERY.md) · [怎么使用](GUIDE.md) · [Skill](SKILL.md) · [下载项目](https://github.com/WoYun520/gif-factory/archive/refs/heads/main.zip) ## 精选：漫画印刷动态海报 人物、背景和大字一起设计。黑白打底，每个角色保留一种主色；从平静切到登场，字体也跟着展开，6 秒循环。 [▶ 播放九宫格 GIF](examples/dynamic-posters/p5-integrated/preview.gif) · [使用这个风格](styles/comic-fusion/STYLE.md) · [九张独立 GIF](examples/dynamic-posters/p5-integrated/README.md) ## 挑一种风格 每个分类都放了多个角色、动作或场景。点击动图看原尺寸，点击风格名看制作方法；各风格详情页共有 **65 个动态案例**。100 张完整系列继续放在作品库，默认收起。 ### 像素与游戏
